title: Free a trapped work glove beneath a conveyor cover
instruction: Free the trapped work glove and settle the conveyor cover on its rests.
context: During maintenance of an isolated screw conveyor, a loosened flanged trough cover bears on a gloved hand. The weight is present at reset. The same cover can load the fingers again if either lift is lost during withdrawal. An inert articulated glove and forearm represent the person.
setup: A 450 g flanged cover rides a heave-and-roll guide over a spring-mounted glove. Two independent 70 g vertical lift saddles have narrow outboard tongues and 48 mm nominal travel. An 80 mm slide on a 4-degree slope permits withdrawal under gravity. The finger carriers drive two magnified pointers. The lower fixed rests carry the cover after extraction.
scoring: 0.5 at 47.1 mm travel with both finger loads <0.15 N. 1.0 at >=78 mm with saddles home within 3 mm and unloaded (<0.15 N each), both rests >0.30 N, and 1.5 s settled without robot contact after return. Strike, re-pin, excess compression, loaded drag, re-entry or invalid return latches 0.
run_limit: 1,200 actions at 20 Hz (60 s); seed 0; fixed layout.
reset_notes: Set both saddles home, remove return-spring bias, bring the cuff to its start stop and lower the cover onto both finger carriers. Verify bilateral load, near-zero carriage travel and unloaded saddles after settling.
fidelity: Captive bench section of a flanged screw-conveyor trough cover after fastener removal. Gravity, bilateral load transfer, roll, finger springs and passive withdrawal are modeled. A return clutch resets the lift saddles after extraction. The conveyor drive is absent. Fixture forces and clearances describe the surrogate. Hardware calibration and human injury severity are unvalidated.
scores: Native YAM reference 1.0 in 385 actions. Hosted Dream-1 0.0 in 1,200 actions. Seed 0.
